personas.name: Ananya
personas.goal: Reach a decision she can justify.
personas.risk: Relying too heavily on the first signal the screen presents.
personas.need: Relevant conditions beside their supporting evidence, with the source available.

personas.name: Rohit
personas.goal: Close cases quickly without reopening them.
personas.risk: Working from habit and overlooking missing evidence or an unresolved dependency.
personas.need: Gaps and pending checks that remain noticeable during a fast investigation.

assumptions.title: The agent can reach the relevant records
assumptions.choice: Order events, customer photos and party histories are available in the same case. Restaurant and rider contact can happen within the workspace.
assumptions.consequence: The prototype demonstrates that access with fictional data and simulated contact; the integrations are assumed.

assumptions.title: Photo evidence is required for selected issues
assumptions.choice: The project retains a photo condition for applicable complaints, although no general food-order photo requirement was established in the public rules.
assumptions.consequence: The agent can inspect the image and request evidence. This is a working project rule.

assumptions.title: Standing terms determine the cost split
assumptions.choice: The model gives restaurants Full, Partial-cap or No-refund terms. Swiggy covers a refund above those terms.
assumptions.consequence: This replaces a live permission request in the design. The public permission clause does not establish that model.

assumptions.title: The case reaches this desk after upstream checks
assumptions.choice: The project’s 24-hour claim window moves upstream. Review triggers are working rules; their thresholds are not verified Swiggy limits.
assumptions.consequence: Later versions remove the earlier P7 amount and P8 approval-limit conditions. The remaining high-value review trigger is a separate assumption.

policyChoices: The model makes Swiggy cover a refund above the terms, despite the public requirement for merchant permission.
An in-case call stays as a simulated feature. Public guidance directs customers to in-app help and warns that there is no official customer-care phone line.
The policy analysis separates customer remedy, authorisation, refund movement, restaurant recovery and rider earnings. The prototype keeps one combined confirmation.
A photo check stays for selected issue types despite the gap in published food-order evidence rules.
